abstentions: Whether rewrite_component_item preserves the SpecItem::Action variant for Action inputs, which determines if the unreachable!() in sync_action is actually safe.
Whether parse_component rejects nested compose inputs, as the documented contract claims but the logic is outside the projected windows.
Whether free (unprefixed) variable names shared across components are intended as global sharing or represent a latent name collision.

findings.description: rewrite_expr guards Expr::Var with `!bound.contains(&name)` before prefixing (lines 711-717), but rewrite_lvalue (687-698) threads `bound` into the recursion yet rewrite_state_name (700-706) never consults it. Trigger: inside a ForAll whose binder name shadows a component state name, an lvalue (LValue::Var or LValue::Index) on that name is prefixed to `alias.<name>` on the assignment target while the same name in an expression stays unqualified, producing inconsistent/corrupted rewrites (e.g. `x[i] = x` where `x` is the binder). The presence of `bound` as a parameter to rewrite_lvalue suggests the check was intended but dropped.
findings.title: rewrite_lvalue ignores the bound set, mis-qualifying shadowed state names

findings.description: At lines 1051-1058, sync_action pattern-matches rewrite_component_item's result on SpecItem::Action with an `else { unreachable!() }`. The input is selected as an Action (line 1034), so this is safe only if rewrite_component_item preserves the Action variant — a behavior outside this projection. If it ever maps an Action to a non-Action, the process panics/aborts, violating the documented contract that lower_compose returns CoreError for invalid inputs rather than aborting.
findings.title: sync_action uses unreachable!() which can abort instead of returning CoreError

findings.description: init_meta is set only while `init_meta.is_none()` (lines 320-322 for component inits, 346-348 for compose-level inits). When several components each declare init metadata, only the first component's meta survives in the merged SpecItem::Init (360-364); later meta is silently dropped without error or warning, which can lose per-component init provenance in the composed kernel.
findings.title: init metadata uses first-wins, silently discarding later components' init meta

summary: Bounded review of lower_compose over target body, statement rewrite, and sync alias boundary. Found a bound-set gap in lvalue name rewriting that can mis-qualify shadowed state names, an unreachable!() panic path in sync_action that bypasses the documented CoreError contract, and first-wins init metadata that silently discards later components' init meta. Callee bodies are absent, so several claims are contingent on unverified behavior.
